name: Welding cell model
summary: The welding cell for EsaSim's 3D view: the four KUKA KR 210 robots with their swan-neck torches and the car body frame on its sled, one model with each part in its own material.
help: Wire the welding-cell-models dataset to Models and the Robot model output to a 3D view and to the Welding cell block's Robot model input (so the welding starts after it); wire the Welding cell block's telemetry to the same view (channels joints, scene, event). The cell is one model: the view moves the sled and the car (joints 1-6) and every robot (its heading, axes A1-A6, then the same undone before the next robot) with the angles of the joints channel; the model's joint list tells the Welding cell block what each angle is. Around them: one red I-beam rail standing on plates bolted to the floor, the sled (a thick deck on two carriages clamped to the beam) and the robots' bases (black steel blocks square to the rail on floor plates with four big bolts; each robot's own base stands on its block). The car frame is satin-silver steel; as the robots weld, dark weld beads appear on it right behind each torch and stay there until the car has left, and a glow at each wire shows the arc. Robot parts keep their glTF colours and sharp edges (the orange glossy under a clear coat), without the cover box on top of the forearm, the wire feeder and the hose. For a 3D view that reads them, the model also says which parts are metal (metalness, roughness, clear coat), that the car mirrors the cell (a cube map), where the arcs are (sparks, light, smoke) and the hall the cell stands in (walls, roof, lamps, a polished floor).

inputs.label: Models
inputs.help: The welding-cell-models dataset: kr210_weld.glb (the robot) and s15_frame.glb (the car frame); without them, boxes stand in

outputs.label: Robot model
outputs.help: welding_cell_all.robot.json.gz (esasim.robot/1 with its joint list, weld beads and arcs): wire it to a 3D view and to the Welding cell block's Robot model input
